answer: Every agent identity is bound to a single hardware TPM chip, and the registry verifier checks its endorsement key against the manufacturer certificate chain before any work counts. A second identity presenting the same chip is rejected and revoked. An honest operator buys one $35 chip once, while an attacker wanting 1,000 fakes must buy 1,000 separate chips for $35,000, because the attestation cannot be copied in software and each fake pays the full hardware price again. A vine crosses the bridge on one thread at a time, and an identity without its own hardware root never gets across.
